authority_basis.claim_scope: Head-to-tail addition, subtraction as addition of the negative vector, and resultant meaning.

concepts.statement: The resultant is the single vector equal to the vector sum of all included vectors.
concepts.why_required: It gives physical meaning to the geometric or component sum.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: A learner may add arrows procedurally without interpreting the net vector.

concepts.statement: Vector subtraction is performed by adding the negative of the vector being subtracted.
concepts.why_required: Subtraction must preserve vector direction semantics.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Magnitude subtraction may be used even when vectors are not collinear.

conditions: Vectors expressed in a common frame
A and B represent commensurate physical quantities

model_conditions.condition: All vectors are expressed in one common reference frame and compatible coordinate convention.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Vector addition combines simultaneous geometric quantities in the same frame.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: The sum can mix incompatible components or physical states.

representations.semantic_geometry: Translate vectors without rotating them so each tail begins at the prior head; the resultant joins the initial tail to the final head.
mandatory_elements: resultant from initial tail to final head
must_not_imply: vector magnitudes can always be added arithmetically
translated vectors have changed physical meaning
representations.verification_method: Compare geometric resultant with an equivalent component sum.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Put all vectors in a common frame before combining them.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Components from incompatible frames may be combined.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: For subtraction reverse the vector being subtracted and treat the operation as addition.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Magnitude subtraction may replace vector subtraction.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Construct or compute the resultant and interpret its physical direction.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The answer remains an uninterpreted algebraic sum.

required_transformations.description: Transform separate vector arrows into a head-to-tail construction that exposes the resultant.
Convert a problem statement into compatible vectors before addition or subtraction.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Vector addition means adding magnitudes regardless of direction.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Scalar arithmetic is more familiar and some collinear examples accidentally reward the shortcut.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Two equal perpendicular vectors produce a resultant of magnitude sqrt(2)A, not 2A.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Use a head-to-tail or component diagram showing directional dependence.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Use vector geometry or components so direction participates in the sum.
misconceptions.verification: Compare the result with the limiting cases of parallel and antiparallel vectors.

problem_families.name: Resultant of multiple vectors
problem_families.first_technical_move: Express all vectors in one common frame.

problem_families.name: Vector difference
problem_families.first_technical_move: Replace subtraction with addition of the reversed vector.
